title: Kernel concierge for bursty traffic with lightweight seqlen estimator and attention-lane optimizations
creator: Aisha Patel
description: We need a lightweight, low-overhead kernel selection agent ("kernel concierge") that runs per-GPU instance and does fast per-request micro-profiling plus a burst-aware sequence-length estimator. The goal is to reduce 95th/99th percentile latency regressions during mixed workloads without heavy offline autotuning or full-stack re-profiling on every deployment. The concierge should: 1) use a tiny sampling prober on a small subset of requests to pick between attention implementations (blockwise, tiled, dense-optimized, quantized fallback), 2) incorporate a short-horizon seqlen predictor trained on request header histograms and recent traffic, 3) decide prefill vs decode kernel split points to reduce tail latency for short-prefill long-decode workloads, and 4) expose a trace tag for rollouts and diagnostics. This ticket scopes the design, prototype, and a non-invasive canary rollout on hosted infra.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype implements a per-GPU agent that samples <=1% of traffic for microbenchmarks and logs selection decisions
Seqlen estimator achieves <10% median absolute error on recent traffic traces and is bounded in CPU usage (<2% on inference nodes)
95th percentile latency for mixed short-prefill workloads improves by >=8% in the canary cohort vs baseline for the same model/version
Fallbacks in the concierge prevent any latency degradation >2x for edge cases and are covered by automated tests
Logs include kernel_choice, seqlen_bucket, reason_code, and probe_id for every sampled request and are visualized on the runtime dashboard
tasks: Draft design doc and decision matrix for acceptable microprobe overhead
Implement lightweight microprobe harness and integrate with runtime kernel chooser API
Build a small seqlen estimator using exponential smoothing + histogram bucketing; collect training traces
Add prefill/decode split heuristic and safety throttles to concierge
Create unit and perf tests; run microbench suites on dev GPU farm
Instrument logging and dashboard panels for canary rollout
Run a two-week canary in hosted beta with 5% traffic; collect metrics and iterate

design_notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) full per-model offline tuning vs lightweight online concierge. Chosen: concierge for faster adaptation and lower ops cost.
Microprobe design: warm up with 8 synthetic micro-batches that mimic observed seqlen buckets; measure decode and prefill kernels separately.
Seqlen estimator: use two-tier approach: short-term EWMA for immediate bursts and long-term histogram for bucket priors to avoid cold-start flips.
Safety nets: max_kernels_change_per_minute, probe_rate_decay_on_error, and quantized_fallback enforced to avoid regressions.
Memory/cpu budget: concierge must not exceed 512MB nor 2 CPU threads under typical load; probes limited by rate-limiter tied to tenancy tier.
risks: Probe-induced noise on latency if sampling not isolated; mitigated by in-process probes and strict rate limits
Seqlen estimator mispredicts rare long-tail requests causing suboptimal kernel pick; mitigated by conservative fallback and decaying weight on estimator
Complexity of kernel matrix increases with new implementations (sparse, fused attn); maintainability concern
Telemetry volume increase from per-request tags; will add sampled logging only and aggregated counters
